I have farmed for 50 years, so I do not want to make risky changes. I have well irrigation, so I will rely on stable water and aim for steady yields instead of chasing the highest possible output. For wheat, I will use improved seed, apply enough nitrogen for strong tillering and grain filling, and keep phosphorus and potassium at moderate levels. I will irrigate a few key times and spray only when needed to control the main diseases and insects. After wheat harvest, I will plant maize on the same 8.0 mu. For maize, I will use hybrid seed because it gives me better yield stability, keep fertilizer relatively strong, irrigate during the key growth stages, and do basic pest control. I will use rotary tillage because it is practical for me and suits my usual way of farming. My goal this year is simple: stable management, controlled costs, and dependable grain production from both crops.
